resources.string: CNN-Based Road Accident Detection on Smartphones using in-built IMU sensors with GPS-Based Emergency Alerts

With the steady increase in road accidents and personal safety incidents calls for the development of a reliable, accessible and real-time emergency response systems.
Existing mobile safety applications often suffer from high false-positive rates, high battery drain, and reliance on cloud-based processing which raises privacy concerns. This paper proposes an edge-computing framework for Android devices that prioritizes privacy and robustness, the framework integrates kinematic sensing and acoustic wake-word detection for autonomous accident detection.
The proposed system uses a dual-modal sensing architecture: an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) sensor pipeline utilizing a 3-class Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for crash classification(vehicle accidents, Pedestrian accidents, no-accident) and an acoustic pipeline utilizing a specialized wake-word CNN model with keyword ”Trigger Backup” for voice activation of emergency alerts. A “Two-Window Confirmation” logic is used to reduce false-positives by agreement between consecutive model predictions before dispatching emergency alerts. To maintain battery efficiency and reliability a multi-stage ”gating” mechanism is used to stop computational tasks when device is idle. An IMU sensor motion gate and an acoustic Root Mean Square (RMS) energy gate filter stationary noise and silence, respectively.
Experimental evaluations of the system demonstrates high responsiveness to collision impact events and moderate wake-word detection in noisy environments. The hybrid location module ensures availability by utilizing “Google Play Services” when user is connected to internet and using hardware level “Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS)” when user is offline. By utilizing edge-computing, the proposed system provides a scalable, reliable, and privacy-centric solution for real-time accident detection and personal safety.

1. Initial Setup: Grant necessary permissions (Location, SMS, Microphone, Physical Activity) and add at least one emergency contact in the 'Add Contacts' section.

2. Monitoring: Ensure the 'Guard Service' is active from the dashboard. The app will monitor in the background using IMU and Acoustic sensors.

3. Detection: In case of a crash, the app automatically triggers an alert. You can also say "Trigger Backup" to manually initiate the emergency protocol.

4. Cancellation: A countdown timer allows you to cancel false alarms before SMS alerts are dispatched to your contacts.

5. Manual Alert: Use the SOS button on the home screen or the floating widget for immediate manual assistance.
